tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Glacial Tourism and Management

questions.question: Describe two economic activities in glaciated upland areas. (4 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Tourism is the largest economic activity, with 18 million visitors per year to the Lake District generating £1.4 billion and 18,000 jobs through accommodation, outdoor activities and retail (2 marks). Hill farming (sheep rearing) is the traditional land use, maintaining the open landscape with hardy breeds like Herdwick sheep, though incomes are low and dependent on subsidies (2 marks).

questions.question: Explain why land use conflicts arise in glaciated uplands. (4 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Land use conflicts arise because multiple groups want different things from the same landscape (1 mark). Tourists want access and facilities, creating footpath erosion, traffic congestion and litter that damages the environment (1 mark). questions.question: Using a named glaciated upland area, describe the management strategies used to reduce conflict. (6 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: In the Lake District National Park, the LDNPA manages conflicts through several strategies. The Fix the Fells programme repairs eroded footpaths using stone pitching and geotextile membranes, addressing the conflict between tourist access and landscape protection (1 mark).
